correctness.rationale: The generating product over the two distinguishable colors satisfies B(x)=(1−x)^(-2)B(x²). For each section, the B(x²) factor passes through as B(x); the indicated Vandermonde transformation computes coefficients of the remaining multiplier exactly. I independently rebuilt the full state space using rational multipliers P(x)/(1−x)^d rather than Newton coefficients: the next numerator is the even/odd section of P(x)(1+x)^(d+2), with denominator (1−x)^(d+2). The reproduced graph has 100 states; its histograms at depths 11 and 12 are (66,62,65,67,63,64,62,62) and (130,126,129,131,127,128,126,126), and all 800 consecutive recurrence residuals vanish in dimension 100. Taking predecessor closures of both labels gives 37 unstable states; exactly ten paths reach unstable states at depth seven and the next 100 differences vanish. Cayley–Hamilton applied to the integer transition matrix extends both identities to all later depths. The ten paths bound the change under any higher digits; together with the −2 offset they give error at most 12 per aligned dyadic block of length ≥2^11. Binary decomposition gives ordinary discrepancy O(1+log X), including real cutoffs by rounding. Positive values 112 mod 128 are 4²(8u+7), so the full obstruction lower density is at least 1/32, not necessarily exactly 1/32.
residual_risks: Only eight residues are classified; the natural density of the entire obstruction set is not decided.

evidence: The general-color automaticity theorem includes m=2, but the published exact obstruction densities are for m=2^k−1. The five-color record proves 1/32 for a different obstruction subset using Thue–Morse congruences.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither color family includes two. Automaticity permits computing the two-color histogram but does not give the eight offsets, the density constant, or an O(log X) bound for arbitrary prefixes.

evidence: A171238 counts binary partitions with two kinds of parts. Sobolewski–Ulas formulate modular coefficient automaticity and their residue question. Gawron–Miska–Ulas establish constant valuations on selected arithmetic progressions.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The color, generating-function coefficient, and fixed-output automaton descriptions refer to the same sequence. A valuation loses the odd-part information distinguishing 112 from 16,48,80, and only the exact residue output distribution gives the present counts.

residual_risks: Uninspected calculations for binary automatic coefficient sequences might implicitly cover a residue statistic; the conclusion is limited to the comparisons made.

value.rationale: This is a motivated modulus and fiber: a single congruence yields a three-square obstruction and directly improves the earlier bound from 1/64 to 1/32. The stabilization and bounded number of suffixes sensitive to high digits give a quantitative all-prefix answer rather than just a dyadic-limit census.
